newsitem.title: USA: Anaconda sets $400 mln junk bonds for mine.
newsitem.headline: Anaconda sets $400 mln junk bonds for mine.

text.p: Anaconda Nickel Ltd plans to raise $400 million for the Murrin Murrin mining project in Western Australia through an offering of high-yield securities in the U.S. in the next several weeks, market sources said.
Murrin Murrin will be the fifth-largest nickel mine and the second-largest cobalt mine in the world when completed in 1999, said sources familiar with the deal.

Proceeds will finance the bulk of Anacanda's contribution to Murrin Murrin, a joint venture between the Australian mining company and Glencore International AG, a privately-held Swiss metals trading company.

Anaconda owns 60 percent of Murrin Murrin while Glencore owns 40 percent. They have agreed to contribute a total of $925 million toward developing the mine and building a processing plant and nickel refinery, sources said.
NatWest Captal Markets Ltd, the investment banking subsidiary of National Westminster Bank Plc will be the sole underwriter of the transaction.

The deal will consist of two tranches: $300 million in fixed-rate 10-year senior secured notes, non-callable for five years and $100 million in floating-rate nine-year senior secured notes, known as a "B-tranche."

The B-tranche, an innovative structure which shares features of both a junk bond and a leveraged loan, is immediately callable and ammortizes according to a fixed-rate shedule. The ammortization rate may be accelerated if the company meets certain cash-flow targets.
Sources said the use of the B-tranche structure will allow the company to achieve a higher credit rating on the transaction and avoid Austalian withholding taxes on interest.
The securities will be issued by Murrin Murrin Holdings Private Ltd and secured by Anaconda's 60 percent ownership interest in the project.
Sources said the securities will be sold via a 144A private placement that will be targeted to U.S. investors, although Australian banks are also expected to be buyers.
